identity.real_world_identity_notes: The Assetto Corsa EVO roster identifies the content as Honda S-2000 (2003). Honda's exact 2003 archive identifies the production S2000 as type LA-AP1 and documents the F20C engine, six-speed manual, dry single-plate diaphragm clutch, constant-mesh transmission, and floor-shift operation. This is the road-going 2003 AP1 S2000, not the later AP2/F22C configuration, an AP1 facelift from another model year, a Type V with variable-ratio steering, or an aftermarket/race conversion.

The official Assetto Corsa EVO roster supplies the exact model year, and Honda's 2003 model archive independently supplies the AP1 type code and production specifications. The 2003 Honda owner's manual supplies exact-year operating instructions for the manual transmission.

claims.basis: The official Assetto Corsa EVO roster supplies the exact model year, and Honda's 2003 model archive independently supplies the AP1 type code and production specifications. The 2003 Honda owner's manual supplies exact-year operating instructions for the manual transmission.

Honda explicitly instructs the driver to push the clutch pedal all the way down when shifting up or down. Honda's 2003 specification lists a six-speed manual transmission, and the owner's manual identifies the six-speed manual and its first-through-sixth shift sequence. Honda's 2003 specification calls the transmission constant-mesh, and the 2003 owner's manual explicitly says the manual transmission is synchronized in all forward gears. Honda specifies floor-shift operation, and the exact-year owner's manual documents the manual gearshift lever's multi-plane gate and reverse lockout. Together these establish a driver-operated H-pattern floor shifter rather than a sequential or paddle system. The 2003 owner's manual's gearshift-lever section identifies the six forward gears in the conventional 1-2 through 5-6 gate and separately describes reverse beside the neutral gate, establishing the standard H pattern. Honda's exact-year starting procedure requires the clutch pedal to be pushed all the way down before the engine can be started, and the car uses a conventional dry manual clutch. Honda explicitly states that the clutch pedal must be pushed all the way down when shifting up or down. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/integrated_display, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

The reviewed sources establish a synchronised six-speed gearbox. Synchronisers match the shaft speeds themselves, so the blip eases them rather than engaging the gear, and the value follows from the construction this record already establishes. AC EVO refuses the shift without a blip, which is carried as a simulator override rather than as the real car.
